name: Palmitoyl oligopeptide

card.summary: A generic palmitoylated peptide label in anti-ageing creams, with no clinical trial of its own.

quick.overview:
Palmitoyl oligopeptide is an ingredient-list term for short peptides attached to a fatty acid, used in anti-ageing creams.

No dedicated clinical trial was found.
quick.mechanism: Formulators describe such peptides as promoting collagen synthesis; the fatty chain is intended to aid skin penetration.
quick.risks: No specific harms were found in the sources reviewed.

lead: Palmitoyl oligopeptide is an ingredient-list name for a short chain of amino acids attached to palmitic acid, a 16-carbon fatty acid, used in anti-ageing creams and serums. Brands include it to help skin look firmer and smoother, with fine lines softened, by acting as a collagen-promoting signal ingredient in the skin's dermis; the fatty chain is meant to help the peptide cross the skin's lipid barrier [1][2][3].

The term is a generic name rather than a single molecule, so what a product contains depends on the formulator. A 2021 analysis of 88 facial cosmetics for sensitive skin from multinational brands found peptides in 17 percent of them and listed seven peptide ingredients, among them palmitoyl oligopeptide, palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, palmitoyl tripeptide-5 and palmitoyl tripeptide-8 [1]. Cosmetic patents list fatty-acid-grafted peptides, specifically C16 palmitoyl oligopeptides, among agents said to promote collagen synthesis [3].

Published research specific to the ingredient is small. A 2015 study from a cosmetic-science group tested a blend of palmitoyl oligopeptide and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 and reported that the blend improved dermal matrix structure compared with placebo and reduced the thickness of a low-echogenic band under the epidermis [2].

chain: Palmitoylated peptide applied in a cream or serum
Fatty chain helps it pass the skin lipid barrier; peptide acts as a signal for matrix renewal
More collagen and matrix structure supports smoother, firmer-looking skin
angle.text: People use creams and serums containing palmitoyl peptides to soften fine lines and firm the look of ageing skin over weeks of daily use. Brands position the ingredient as a signal that encourages skin to rebuild its own collagen matrix.

paras: Palmitoyl oligopeptide appears in anti-ageing formulations and in sensitive-skin products that contain synthetic peptides [1][3]. Patent compositions pair palmitoyl oligopeptide with other actives, for example amber extract, magnesium aspartate and peptides that act on muscle contraction, describing it as a fatty-acid-grafted peptide that promotes collagen synthesis [3][4].

Formulators describe palmitoylated peptides as signal peptides, short fragments that tell skin cells to make more extracellular matrix such as collagen. The palmitic acid chain is added to make the peptide more lipophilic and thereby more able to penetrate the stratum corneum [1]. The related and better-known palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl, Pal-KTTKS) was launched by Sederma in 2000 and is described on Wikipedia as a matrikine, with the mechanism claim noted as needing medical citation [5].

The 2021 review of cosmetics for sensitive skin concluded that only five of the seven peptides it listed had evidence supporting use in sensitive skin, that only one clinical study included volunteers with sensitive skin, and that most data came from patents and supplier brochures rather than randomised placebo-controlled trials [1].

The 2015 Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology study (Mondon et al.) developed a method combining mass spectrometric imaging, reflectance confocal microscopy, echography and histology. It found most selected dermal and junction proteins less abundant in aged skin explants than young, and reported that a palmitoyl oligopeptide plus palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 blend improved extracellular matrix structure against placebo and increased the density of the subepidermal band on echography. The authors called their imaging work preliminary [2].
No studies found testing palmitoyl oligopeptide alone in a clinical trial. The 2015 study tested it as part of a blend with palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 [2].

timeline.event: Sederma launches palmitoyl pentapeptide Matrixyl, a related palmitoylated cosmetic peptide.[5]
